request: Remind requesters when a ticket has been waiting on them for too long.

labels.why: None of the four statuses explicitly means the requester owes an action, so the worker needs an observable condition with defined entry and exit events.
The worker needs a threshold and a start time for each wait, including whether priority affects the threshold, because unrelated edits also advance updated.
An overdue ticket can qualify on every worker tick, so a count, spacing rule and stopping condition determine how many messages its requester receives.

labels.applies_part: Define which recorded ticket changes end the wait, including which transition can stand for a requester response and whether an ordinary agent edit affects eligibility.
labels.why: The store observes edits and transitions, while detecting a reply independently of a recorded ticket change would require a new inbound channel.
The notifier needs a subject, body and recipient, and a valid ticket can contain a requester name that the mail relay cannot address.
The resolved notice already tells the requester to reply within seven days, so the reminder needs consistent instructions for an action the help desk can honor.
The service assigns scheduled work to a single worker that runs jobs in order, so its tick schedule and job order determine when reminders are queued and delivered.
The outbox releases a key after delivery, while the relay deduplicates retries by key and event ID, so one scheduled reminder needs a stable identity across ticks and restarts.
A ticket can leave the waiting condition after it was last checked, so the store must use its current state when deciding whether to enqueue.
A missing template fails at delivery today, so the reminder needs a defined template, retry policy and outcome for later ticks once an event is dead.
The first worker tick after deployment can encounter tickets that have already waited past the threshold, making their initial eligibility a rollout decision.
A reopened ticket keeps its ID and outbox history, so a later wait needs a rule for carrying over or restarting the clock, count and reminder keys.

labels.applies_part: Define the clock, time zone and exact threshold comparison, including when a ticket first qualifies under an elapsed-time rule.
labels.why: The service supplies a clock and UTC timestamps, while holding delivery for business hours or holidays would add calendar-aware scheduling.
Restart behavior depends on where the worker recovers the start of a wait and prior reminders, and the data file keeps only explicitly serialized record fields.
Existing deployments must load their current data files, and the loader must distinguish an absent legacy field from an invalid stored value and identify the latter.
The store audits ticket mutations and records deliveries separately, so the specification must say whether a reminder changes the ticket and what timestamp, actor and action follow.

labels.applies_part: Identify who controls the deployment settings and which existing ticket actions stop eligibility, accounting for the fact that clients supply their own X-Actor value.
labels.why: Operators already control the process environment, while sending or cancelling an individual reminder by hand would require a new control.
The service reads settings from the environment and reports invalid values by name, and operators rely on WORKER_INTERVAL_MS=0 to stop all scheduled work.
The outbox already shows sent events and pending attempts with their due times, and the weekly report relies on the positions of the CLI's raw columns.
The reminder check shares a synchronous worker with delivery, so batch size and scan cost govern both lateness under load and how long existing notifications wait.
Reminders share the ticket store, worker and persisted records with existing callers, so lifecycle, notification, API, audit and reporting contracts all matter to regression coverage.
The manual clock makes reminder timing testable, the API and operator docs describe affected behavior, and the contribution guide specifies release updates and decision records.
